description: Experience the true taste of Liguria with this authentic Focaccia Genovese, a delightful flatbread known for its crispy crust and tender, airy interior. Infused with aromatic rosemary and rich olive oil, it is perfect as an appetizer, side dish, or light meal. This traditional recipe brings the essence of Italian baking right into your home kitchen.

ingredients.notes: plus more for drizzling and pan

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and active dry yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active. This step is crucial for a good rise.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Drizzle in 2 tablespoons of the olive oil and knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for about 8-10 minutes until it is smooth and elastic. It should be slightly sticky.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until it has doubled in size. This slow rise develops flavor.

instructions.title: Shape and Dimple
instructions.text: Generously oil a 9x13 inch baking pan with olive oil. Gently transfer the risen dough to the pan. Using your fingertips, gently stretch and press the dough to fill the pan, creating characteristic dimples across the surface. Do not punch down too hard.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Bake Prep
instructions.text: Drizzle the top of the dough with more olive oil, sprinkle with fresh rosemary leaves and coarse sea salt. Cover loosely and let it rise again for another 30-45 minutes in a warm place. Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F) during the last 15 minutes of this rise.

instructions.title: Bake to Golden Perfection
instructions.text: Bake the focaccia in the preheated oven for 20-30 minutes, or until it is golden brown on top and cooked through. The bottom should also be nicely browned and crispy. Once baked, remove from the oven, drizzle immediately with a little more extra virgin olive oil, and let it cool slightly before slicing and serving. Enjoy the aroma!

tips: For the best texture, ensure your kitchen is warm during the rising stages. A slightly humid environment helps the dough stay moist and rise beautifully.
Do not skimp on the olive oil. It is crucial for the authentic flavor, golden crust, and crispy bottom of true Focaccia Genovese. Use a good quality extra virgin olive oil.
Store leftover focaccia at room temperature covered with a clean cloth for up to 2 days, or freeze slices for longer preservation. Reheat gently in an oven or toaster oven for best results.
article:
Focaccia, the beloved flatbread of Italy, holds a special place in the hearts and ovens of bakers worldwide. Among its many regional variations, one stands out for its delicate crumb, crisp crust, and intoxicating aroma: Focaccia Genovese. Hailing from the picturesque Ligurian capital of Genoa, this particular focaccia is a masterclass in simplicity and flavor, often graced with fragrant rosemary and a generous drizzle of the finest olive oil. It’s more than just bread; it’s an edible piece of Italian history, a testament to the region’s culinary heritage and its bountiful olive groves.

Making authentic Focaccia Genovese at home is a deeply rewarding experience. It's a journey that transforms humble ingredients into a golden, airy masterpiece, perfect for tearing, dipping, and savoring. This guide will walk you through the secrets of achieving that perfect texture and taste, ensuring your kitchen is filled with the irresistible scent of Italian baking.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?

At its core, Focaccia Genovese is a flatbread characterized by its exceptionally airy, open crumb, a thin, crispy bottom, and a signature dimpled surface that cradles pools of olive oil and coarse sea salt. Unlike some thicker, denser focaccia varieties found across Italy, the Genovese version is typically flatter, emphasizing its light texture and the interplay of salt and oil. Its history stretches back centuries, with various theories suggesting its origins as a simple unleavened bread cooked on hearths or coals, evolving over time into the yeast-leavened delicacy we know today.

In Genoa, focaccia is not just an accompaniment; it's a staple. Locals enjoy it at breakfast with coffee, as a snack, or alongside meals. The key to its distinct character lies in a high-hydration dough, a significant amount of high-quality extra virgin olive oil both in the dough and on top, and a careful baking process that ensures a golden-brown exterior and a remarkably soft interior. The rosemary and coarse sea salt are traditional toppings, adding an aromatic depth and a delightful crunch that elevates every bite.

## Ingredients for Rosemary Olive Oil Focaccia

Crafting the perfect Focaccia Genovese starts with selecting the right ingredients. Quality truly matters here, especially for the olive oil.

*   **Strong Bread Flour:** Approximately 500g. Bread flour has a higher protein content, which is essential for developing the strong gluten network needed to achieve focaccia's characteristic chewy yet airy texture. All-purpose flour can work, but the result might be slightly less airy.
*   **Lukewarm Water:** About 400ml. The high hydration is crucial for a tender crumb. Ensure the water is lukewarm (around 105-115°F or 40-46°C) to properly activate the yeast.
*   **Active Dry Yeast:** 7g (1 packet). This will give your focaccia its lift. Instant yeast can also be used, in which case you can mix it directly with the flour.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** 10g (about 1.5 teaspoons) for the dough. Salt is vital for flavor and also helps control yeast activity.
*   **High-Quality Extra Virgin Olive Oil (EVOO):** 60ml for the dough, plus plenty more for the pan, dimpling, and finishing. This is perhaps the most critical ingredient. A good quality EVOO will impart a fruity, peppery depth that defines the flavor of Focaccia Genovese. Do not skimp here!
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** 2-3 sprigs, needles stripped and roughly chopped, for topping. Fresh is best for its vibrant aroma.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt:** For sprinkling generously over the top before baking. This provides a delightful textural contrast and burst of salinity.
*   **Optional: A pinch of sugar (about 1 teaspoon):** To help activate the yeast, especially if you're unsure of its freshness.

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Focaccia Genovese

Patience is a virtue in baking, and focaccia is no exception. Follow these steps for a truly authentic result.

**1. Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water, yeast, and optional pinch of sugar. Stir gently and let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. This indicates the yeast is active.

**2. Mix the Dough:** To the foamy yeast mixture, add the fine sea salt and 60ml of extra virgin olive oil. Gradually add the flour, mixing with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy, sticky dough forms. Do not knead at this stage; just ensure all the flour is incorporated. The dough will be very wet – this is correct!

**3. First Rise (Bulk Fermentation with Folds):** Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel and let it rest in a warm place for 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, perform a series of "stretch and folds." With wet hands, gently grab a portion of the dough from one side, stretch it upwards, and fold it over itself towards the center. Rotate the bowl and repeat this process 3-4 times, covering all sides. This develops gluten without traditional kneading. Repeat this stretch-and-fold process every 30 minutes for a total of 2-3 times (over 1.5 - 2 hours). After the last fold, let the dough rise undisturbed for another 1-2 hours, or until it has roughly doubled in size and is bubbly.

**4. Prepare the Pan:** Generously drizzle about 3-4 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil into a 9x13-inch (23x33 cm) baking pan. Ensure the entire bottom and sides are coated.

**5. Transfer and Dimple:** Gently scrape the risen dough into the prepared pan. With oiled hands, gently stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. Once stretched, use your fingertips to create deep dimples all over the surface of the dough. These dimples are essential for focaccia's signature look and for holding the olive oil. Drizzle another generous amount of extra virgin olive oil (2-3 tablespoons) over the dimpled surface, ensuring it pools in the crevices. Sprinkle evenly with the chopped fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt.

**6. Second Rise (Proofing):** Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel and let the Focaccia Genovese proof for another 30-45 minutes in a warm spot. It should look puffy and slightly expanded.

**7. Bake:** Preheat your oven to a high temperature, around 425°F (220°C). Bake the focaccia for 20-30 minutes, or until it is deeply golden brown on top and the bottom is crisp. The baking time can vary, so keep an eye on it.

**8. Finish and Serve:** As soon as you remove the focaccia from the oven, drizzle it with a final flourish of extra virgin olive oil. This adds gloss, moisture, and even more flavor. Let it cool in the pan for a few minutes, then transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly before slicing and serving.

## Expert Tips for Perfect Focaccia

*   **Embrace the Stickiness:** Focaccia dough is high hydration, meaning it's very wet and sticky. Resist the urge to add more flour, as this will result in a dry, dense focaccia. Oiled hands are your friend!
*   **Quality EVOO is Non-Negotiable:** Seriously, invest in a good bottle. It makes all the difference in flavor.
*   **Don't Skimp on Salt:** Both in the dough and on top. The coarse sea salt provides a textural contrast that is heavenly.
*   **Deep Dimples:** Really press your fingers into the dough to create those signature pockets. This helps the olive oil penetrate and creates a beautiful texture.
*   **Listen to Your Dough:** Pay attention to its rise and feel. If it needs a little longer to proof, give it time. Rushing leads to a less airy crumb.
*   **Hot Oven, Crispy Crust:** The high oven temperature is crucial for achieving that desirable crispy crust and a rapid rise.
*   **Cool Slightly:** While tempting to devour immediately, letting it cool for 10-15 minutes allows the internal structure to set, making it easier to slice and improving the texture.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Focaccia

Focaccia Genovese is incredibly versatile. Here are just a few ways to enjoy your freshly baked masterpiece:

*   **Plain and Simple:** Its pure flavor is captivating enough to be enjoyed on its own, perhaps with a glass of wine.
*   **Dipping:** Serve with a small bowl of high-quality extra virgin olive oil and balsamic vinegar for dipping.
*   **Appetizer:** Pair with olives, cured meats (like prosciutto or salami), and a selection of Italian cheeses.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice it horizontally and fill with your favorite deli meats, cheeses, roasted vegetables, or pesto for an epic sandwich.
*   **Alongside Meals:** It makes a wonderful accompaniment to soups, stews, salads, or pasta dishes, perfect for soaking up delicious sauces.
*   **Breakfast:** In Genoa, it's often enjoyed with coffee or cappuccino in the morning. A delicious, if unconventional, start to the day!

## Variations & Substitutions for Focaccia Genovese

While the rosemary and olive oil version is classic, Focaccia Genovese is also a fantastic canvas for culinary creativity.

*   **Other Herbs:** Experiment with fresh thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs instead of or in addition to rosemary.
*   **Tomatoes:** Press cherry tomatoes (halved or whole) into the dimples before baking. They burst with flavor.
*   **Olives:** Kalamata, Castelvetrano, or any pitted olives can be pressed into the dough for a briny kick.
*   **Onions:** Thinly sliced red or white onions, sometimes caramelized first, can be spread over the top.
*   **Garlic:** Thinly sliced garlic or roasted garlic cloves can be added for a pungent aroma.
*   **Cheese:** A sprinkle of grated Parmesan, Pecorino, or even dollops of soft stracchino cheese can be added during the last few minutes of baking.
*   **Pesto:** After baking, spread a thin layer of pesto over the warm focaccia for an explosion of basil flavor.
*   **Anchovies:** For the truly traditional and adventurous, small pieces of anchovies can be pressed into the dimples before baking.

Mastering the art of Focaccia Genovese is a delightful journey into the heart of Italian baking. With its inviting aroma, crisp exterior, and tender, olive oil-infused interior, this bread is more than just food; it's an experience. So roll up your sleeves, gather your finest ingredients, and prepare to bake a piece of Ligurian sunshine right in your own kitchen. Buon appetito!
